objects.summary: Source-grounded transition checklist for a newly certified Nebraska assessor, excluding internal county procedures and private paperwork until those materials are provided.
objects.plain_language: A first pass at what must be legally and operationally ready before the office starts moving under your name.

steps.step: Confirm county assessor certificate status and recertification horizon.
Complete oath and bond prerequisites before entering duties.
Map statutory duty inventory: assessment roll, record review, real property revision, omitted property, preliminary meetings if applicable, and obedience to Tax Commissioner/TERC rules and orders.
Load the PAD calendar, county reports calendar, county clerk/BOE calendar, treasurer calendar, homestead calendar, and education calendar into a working command calendar.
Inventory open statutory deadlines, open appeals, pending BOE/TERC matters, pending valuation notices, pending exemptions, and reports due to PAD.
Apply Schedule 14 records-retention triage before disposing, archiving, or reorganizing inherited records.
Reserve internal extension points for CAMA access, parcel/deed workflow, sales validation, field-review packets, BOE packets, TERC exhibits, staff roles, and public-records intake.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska Secretary of State Records Management Division, Schedule 14 County Assessors.

objects.summary: Procedure for routing assessor records through Schedule 14 retention, appeal/audit/request holds, state archives review where required, and documented disposition.
objects.plain_language: Before deleting, moving, or boxing inherited office records, classify them and check for appeals, audits, requests, and Schedule 14 retention rules.

steps.step: Classify each record series under Schedule 14 or the Local Agencies General Records Schedule if Schedule 14 does not cover it.
Check for pending or ongoing appeal, legal action, audit, or records request before disposition.
Apply the longer or more specific retention rule when schedules overlap.
For records requiring State Archives review or transfer, contact State Archives before transfer/disposition.
Complete the required records disposition documentation for destroyed records.
Preserve internal chain-of-custody and CAMA/audit-log references through the final resolution date of any appeal.

object.retention: 4 years after adoption of each new plan
5 years unless appeal pending, then 5 years after final appeal resolution

relationships.note: Property record and audit trail retention.

steps.step: Identify the class/subclass, review area, or inspection route selected for systematic review.
Compare current property record data to observable facts, sales review notes, permits, GIS/deed changes, and prior record-card data.
Record data changes needed for land, improvements, quality, condition, use, occupancy, physical characteristics, and relevant valuation influences.
Document reasons for deviations from standard manuals, schedules, or tables where applicable.
Update CAMA/property record fields and preserve the workpaper or audit trail supporting the change.
Route taxpayer communication, access/refusal handling, photo policy, safety procedure, and county form packets through future internal workflow inserts.

objects.canonical_term: Board of Equalization and County Board Question Bank
objects.summary: Core public-law Q&A frames for county board, board of supervisors, and board of equalization questions about valuation protests, equalization, evidence, taxes versus value, and appeal routing.
objects.plain_language: This helps board members stay in the right lane: value/equalization evidence, not general tax frustration.

object.q: What is the board deciding in a valuation protest?
object.answer_frame: Current-year assessment/equalization issue for the described property, not the taxpayer's overall tax affordability.

object.q: Can the board raise as well as lower value?
object.answer_frame: Route to board statutory powers and due process/notice requirements before answering from local facts.

object.q: What evidence should matter?
object.answer_frame: Evidence tied to actual value, comparable properties, equalization, classification, property record accuracy, or a specific legal program.

object.q: How should tax-bill complaints be handled?
object.answer_frame: Explain value versus levy/tax request mechanics and route levy questions to budget/taxing-subdivision context.

object.q: What must be preserved for appeal?
object.answer_frame: Decision, notice, protest form, exhibits, property record, assessor analysis, board/referee report, and appeal deadline trace.

object.q: What if a taxpayer presents a recent appraisal?
object.answer_frame: Treat it as evidence; compare effective date, property rights, scope, market period, and whether it addresses the assessment date and issue.

object.q: What if a taxpayer says neighbors are lower?
object.answer_frame: Route to equalization: identify truly comparable parcels and whether equivalent characteristics receive equivalent treatment.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska DOR, Nebraska Property Assessment FAQs.

objects.summary: Core Q&A frames for preparing taxpayers, assessors, and boards for the post-BOE TERC appeal stage.
objects.plain_language: This keeps the next-step appeal questions tied to evidence, deadlines, forms, and record preservation.

object.q: What do I file after a county board decision?
object.answer_frame: Use the TERC appeal form, required fee, and copy of the decision being appealed; verify current deadline for the tax year and county.

object.q: Can I use the county protest form as the TERC appeal?
object.answer_frame: No; TERC identifies its own appeal form as separate from the county board protest form.

object.q: What should the assessor preserve after a BOE decision?
object.answer_frame: Preserve decision, notices, protest, property record, evidence, exhibits, analysis, and communications under appeal hold.

object.q: Are hearings informal or formal?
object.answer_frame: TERC states hearings are informal unless a formal hearing is requested; procedure should be checked for the case type.

object.q: Can a TERC decision be appealed further?
object.answer_frame: TERC notes final Commission decisions may be appealed to the Nebraska Court of Appeals under the applicable statute.

relationships.note: Regular valuation appeal follows BOE decision.
